patch.value: GH-1179: legacy merge-receipt shape is misclassified as a gate-failing missing history reference with no remedy

GitHub issue #1179 reproduces on pm-cli 2026.9.2: merge receipts already present in merge_reconcile history are classified as merge_receipt_history_reference_missing when they use the supported older shape with preferred and without conflict_resolution. The gate-failing remediation only re-reads health, while pm merge reconcile reports no drift and no work, leaving historical repositories permanently unable to satisfy strict health.

Normalize or explicitly version the preferred-era receipt shape at the compatibility boundary; never classify a present receipt as a missing reference solely because newer fields are absent; downgrade genuinely unverifiable legacy evidence to a truthful advisory or provide an audited state-changing migration; ensure every gate-failing remediation can progress state; add old/new mixed-history integration and strict-exit negative controls; pass merge, health, SDK, CLI, security, static, and exact coverage gates.
pm-cli 2026.9.2 reading history with pre-requested_preference merge receipt records

Use a history containing merge_reconcile receipts with preferred but no conflict_resolution, delete the drift cache, run pm health --strict-exit, then run pm merge reconcile --dry-run; observe a gate-failing missing-reference diagnosis although receipt IDs exist and reconcile finds nothing.

Health recognizes every supported legacy receipt epoch or reports a truthful advisory unverifiable-schema classification with an actionable migration, while strict gate failures always name a state-changing remediation.
Every older receipt shape is classified as a missing history reference at gate-failing severity; the suggested diagnostic cannot change state and reconciliation reports zero work.
SDK merge receipt compatibility, health classification, and remediation registry
Repositories that used field-aware merging before the receipt schema change can be permanently blocked from release by an inaccurate, unrepairable integrity verdict.
